subject: Post-demo cost & benchmark: Nimbus Health - pricing validation
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bates <lauren.bates@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo recap + ask: token volumes, budget range, target $/1M

Hi Lauren — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a couple of items we need to lock to produce a short commercial proposal.

Recap (30-min demo):
- Showed inference latency/throughput for clinical summarization flows and secure VPC options.
- Highlighted batching + KV caching that usually drops effective token spend by ~20–40% on repeat summaries.
- Reviewed compliance posture (SOC2 + optional HSM).

Questions / asks to finalize pricing options:
1) Estimated monthly token volume (rough bands OK): low (<=50M), mid (50–500M), high (>500M).
2) Target budget range for inference (monthly) or target $/1M tokens you want us to hit.
3) Required SLA / uptime and whether you need private deployment (VPC/on-prem).

Why this matters: different host & model choices materially change unit economics. For the proposal we’ll include 3 options: Pilot (no commit), Committed Tier (discounted $/1M), and Dedicated (reserved capacity + SLA). Attached is a working pricing grid + a short benchmark snapshot vs OpenAI/Anthropic and a sample open-host.

Suggested next steps:
- You confirm estimated monthly tokens and a budget band by Wednesday 10/6.
- We’ll return a compact commercial that maps to the bands with explicit $/1M targets, projected monthly charges, and pilot acceptance criteria.

Attachments: Redwood_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (workbook), Benchmark_snapshot_OpenHosts_vs_Redwood.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

---
From: Lauren Bates <lauren.bates@nimbushealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: token volumes, budget range, target $/1M

Thanks Priya — quick answers from our side:
- Volume: initial pilot ~15M tokens/mo, goal is to ramp to ~250M tokens/mo over 6–9 months if quality and latency hold.
- Budget: for pilot we have ~$12k–$18k/month allocated; at scale procurement will look for unit economics to be in line with peers.
- Deployment: prefer VPC (data residency); SOC2 required.

Can you show a simple row that maps the pilot (15M) and ramp (250M) to total monthly spend at your proposed $/1M, and highlight how caching or a committed discount moves the effective cost? Procurement looped in — they’ll need the commercial to evaluate quickly.

— Lauren
Director of Product, Nimbus Health
lauren.bates@nimbushealth.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bates <lauren.bates@nimbushealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 16:24:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: token volumes, budget range, target $/1M

Lauren — thanks for the clarity. Per Priya’s ask, I put together a concise mapping below (we’ll include this in the official one-pager). Numbers are illustrative and assume standard chat workloads (mix of short prompts + longer summaries). We also note expected caching benefits for clinical templates.

Baseline host comps (public list prices, per 1M tokens):
- OpenAI (gpt-4 style managed): $1,200 / 1M
- Anthropic (Claude-like managed): $850 / 1M
- Typical open-model host (unmanaged, GPU-backed): $360 / 1M

Redwood proposal mechanics (options):
- Pilot (no commit): $750 / 1M; estimates include basic caching but no reserved capacity.
- Committed Tier (6–12 mo, 50–500M/mo band): $420 / 1M (20% incremental discount at 250M+).
- Dedicated (reserved pool + SLA): list $560 / 1M, with effective $/1M after autoscaling & quantization optimizations typically as low as $260 / 1M for steady-state high-volume workloads.

Mapping to your bands:
- Pilot (15M tokens/mo @ $750): ~$11,250/mo — inside your pilot budget band.
- Ramp (250M tokens/mo):
  - Pilot pricing: $187,500/mo (not appropriate at scale)
  - Committed Tier @ $420: $105,000/mo
  - Dedicated effective (post-optimization) ~$65,000/mo (effective $260/1M)

Key assumptions / notes:
- Caching: we conservatively applied 25% effective token reduction on repeat patient-note templates for the Dedicated scenario.
- Model choice: managed high-capability models (OpenAI/Anthropic) remain higher list prices; Redwood’s Dedicated + open-model hosting with quantization yields the biggest unit savings while preserving throughput.
- SLAs and VPC add operational costs (folded into Dedicated pricing).

Requested next steps from Redwood -> Nimbus:
1) Can procurement confirm pilot acceptance criteria and whether signed NDA + SOC2 evidence suffice for a pilot?
2) If pilot budget is approved (~$12–15k/mo), Priya will produce a 2-page pilot SOW and a short pilot PO / DS for signatures.
3) We’ll prepare a 1-week technical runbook for VPC onboarding if you want to start infra prep in parallel.

I attached an extract from the pricing grid that shows the same numbers side-by-side and a short benchmark PDF comparing latency & unit costs vs the hosts you called out.

If this looks good I’ll convert to a short commercial and send the DocuSign link (we already have your contact in HubSpot).

— Marissa
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
From: Lauren Bates <lauren.bates@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 18:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: token volumes, budget range, target $/1M

This is very helpful — thanks Marissa. Pilot budget approved at $14k/mo (we’ll pay via PO). SOC2 evidence is fine to start; procurement will send a short PO template and signatures request. Please go ahead and send the 2-page SOW + DocuSign for the pilot.

Also: can you add one line in the SOW that shows estimated cost impact if we enable a 30% caching uplift vs the conservative 25% in your table? Procurement asked for a conservative and an optimistic case.

We’re good to start infra prep; I’ll introduce our infra lead if you want to kick off the network checklist.

— Lauren
